## Stage 0 Decisions at a Glance

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| 1 | Analog-matched design, zero latency, no oversampling | Matched pole pairs and matched zero pairs (impulse-invariant, Vicanek 2016 eq. 12) plus a first-order corrector that makes DC and Nyquist gain exact ("matched low-pass ratio", MLR). One designer for every gain-bearing section. Cuts use a 3-point matched low-pass / matched high-pass. First-order shelves use Vicanek 2019. |
| 2 | Matched coefficients vs modulation-safe topology | Every section is realised as a trapezoidal state-variable filter (Simper form) whose 5 parameters (g, k, mL, mB, mH) are a bijection of any stable biquad, plus a TPT one-pole. Double state. Parameters are designed on a fixed 16-sample control grid and interpolated per sample in the (g, k, m) domain, where every interpolant is a stable filter. |
| 3 | Slopes 6-96 dB/oct | Order N = slope / 6. Honoured by Low Cut, High Cut, Low Shelf, High Shelf, Tilt Shelf (Butterworth families, Q = resonance factor on the highest-Q section, Q 1.0 = Butterworth). Inert for Bell, Notch, Band Pass in v1. Type / slope / placement / enable / bypass changes crossfade between two section chains over 20 ms. |
| 4 | Placement with 24 serial bands | Bands run in index order on L/R. Mid and Side bands filter m or s and inject only the difference back into L and R. Inactive bands are skipped, so untouched channels and the all-off case are bit-identical. |
| 5 | True-response display | The message thread runs the same designer on the current parameter values and pushes section parameter sets; JS evaluates the closed-form complex response. No audio-thread hand-off, so the curve updates with the transport stopped. Analyzer: lock-free FIFO, FFT on the message thread at 30 Hz. |
| 6 | Auto gain | Curve-derived: negative of the pink-weighted mean power gain of the target response, 64 log-spaced points 40 Hz - 16 kHz, clamped to -18 / +12 dB, 100 ms ramp, computed on the audio thread. |
| 7 | Dynamic-EQ forward compatibility | The 72 reserved parameters are NOT registered in v1. v1 parameters use `ParameterID { id, 1 }`; dynamic-EQ parameters are added later with version hint 2 under reserved IDs. State carries `stateVersion`. The band engine already takes a per-band gain offset on the control grid. |
| 8 | CPU | 24 bands x 96 dB/oct cut, stereo, 48 kHz = 384 SVF sections per sample. Budget 10 % of one core settled, 35 % with all bands modulating. Inactive bands are not in the active list. SIMD deferred. |
| 9 | Verification | 13 gates with thresholds, section "Verification Gates". |

## Core Components

### 1. Analog Prototype Builder (`eq::Prototype`)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (pure functions, `juce_core` only)
- **Purpose:** Turn one band's settings (type, frequency, effective gain, Q, slope) into a list of analog sections: second-order `(wz, Qz, wp, Qp, scalar)` or first-order `(wz, wp, scalar)`, plus a section class tag.
- **Parameters Affected:** `bNN_type`, `bNN_freq`, `bNN_gain`, `bNN_q`, `bNN_slope`, `gain_scale`
- **Configuration:**
  - Section counts: order N = slope / 6 gives `N / 2` second-order sections plus one first-order section when N is odd. Maximum 8 second-order sections per band.
  - Effective gain `gEff = clamp(gain * gain_scale / 100, -60, +60)` dB.
  - Frequency policy near and above Nyquist: see Algorithm Details.

### 2. Matched Section Designer (`eq::Designer`)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (pure functions; double precision; `std::exp`, `std::expm1`, `std::sin`, `std::tan`, `std::tanh`, `std::sqrt`)
- **Purpose:** Map each analog section to digital section parameters: SVF `(g, k, mL, mB, mH)` and, for gain-bearing sections, a corrector one-pole `(G, cL, cH)`.
- **Parameters Affected:** same as component 1, plus the session sample rate
- **Configuration:**
  - Stateless and reentrant. The audio thread and the message thread each call it; no shared mutable state.
  - Cancellation-free forms are mandatory (see "MatchedPair"). The naive forms lose the 10 Hz / Q 40 case [MODEL].

### 3. Section Engine (`eq::SvfSection`, `eq::OnePole`)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom. `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter` and `juce::dsp::StateVariableTPTFilter` are NOT used (per-instance `ProcessSpec` overhead at up to 768 instances, the first-order default-constructor allocation trap, and no access to mix coefficients).
- **Purpose:** Run the sections. Double-precision state. Two code paths: settled (constant parameters) and ramping (per-sample linear interpolation of the parameter set).
- **Parameters Affected:** none directly
- **Configuration:** trapezoidal SVF in the Simper (Cytomic) form; TPT one-pole; recurrences in Algorithm Details.

### 4. Band Runtime (`eq::Band`)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom
- **Purpose:** One of 24 bands. Owns two slots (A / B), each a full section chain for up to 2 lanes; parameter ramps; the control-grid design step; structural crossfades; neutral-gain sleep.
- **Parameters Affected:** all `bNN_*`, `gain_scale`
- **Configuration:**
  - Continuous parameters (frequency, gain, Q, gain scale): ramped 20 ms at the control grid. Frequency and Q ramp in the log domain, gain in dB.
  - Structural parameters (type, slope, placement, enabled, bypass): 20 ms raised-cosine crossfade between slots.
  - Dynamic-EQ hook: `dynOffsetDb` (double, 0 in v1) is added to `gEff` at every control tick.

### 5. Placement Router (`eq::Router`)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom
- **Purpose:** Apply each band to Stereo, Left, Right, Mid or Side while keeping untouched channels bit-identical.
- **Parameters Affected:** `bNN_placement`
- **Configuration:** difference injection for Mid / Side; see Processing Chain.

### 6. Output Stage (`eq::OutputStage`)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom ramps (not `juce::dsp::Gain`: the unseeded ramp fades in from silence at every `prepareToPlay`, suite lesson)
- **Purpose:** Auto gain, output gain, global soft bypass, output peak meter.
- **Parameters Affected:** `auto_gain`, `output_gain`, `bypass`
- **Configuration:** all gains ramp 20 ms (auto gain 100 ms); a gain of exactly 1.0 that is not ramping is skipped.

### 7. Auto Gain Estimator (`eq::AutoGain`)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom
- **Purpose:** Deterministic curve-derived loudness compensation.
- **Parameters Affected:** `auto_gain`, every band parameter
- **Configuration:** 64 log-spaced points 40 Hz - 16 kHz, per-band cached log-power vectors, re-evaluated at most every 1024 samples at 48 kHz.

### 8. Spectrum Tap and Analyzer (`eq::SpectrumTap`, `SpectrumAnalyzer`)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AbstractFifo` (juce_core), `juce::dsp::FFT`, `juce::dsp::WindowingFunction<float>` (juce_dsp)
- **Purpose:** Pre and post spectrum for the display.
- **Parameters Affected:** none (analyzer mode is UI state)
- **Configuration:** audio thread copies only; FFT on the editor's message-thread timer. No shared module exists for this (checked `modules/registry.yaml` 1.3.2); it is plugin-local and a candidate for later extraction.

### 9. Display Model (`eq::DisplayModel`)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom, plus `juce::WebBrowserComponent::emitEventIfBrowserIsVisible`
- **Purpose:** Produce the section parameter sets the page draws from.
- **Parameters Affected:** all band parameters, `gain_scale`
- **Configuration:** message-thread instance of components 1 and 2.

### 10. Listen Filter (`eq::Listen`) — FUNC-08, should
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (reuses components 2 and 3)
- **Purpose:** Band solo / listen.
- **Parameters Affected:** none (transient UI state `listenBand`, -1 = off; not saved)
- **Configuration:** Bell / Notch / Band Pass: matched band-pass at the band's frequency and Q. Low Shelf / Low Cut: 12 dB/oct matched low-pass at the band frequency. High Shelf / High Cut: 12 dB/oct matched high-pass. Tilt: band-pass, Q 0.7. Placement respected. Output crossfades 20 ms between the EQ path and the listen path.

## Processing Chain

```
Input (float, mono or stereo)
  │
  ├──► Spectrum tap PRE (only if editor open and mode needs it)
  │
  ▼
[fast path]  no active band, no fade, output gain == 1, auto gain == 1, not bypassed
  │            → buffer is not touched (bit-identical)            ← QUAL-01
  ▼
float → double working buffers L, R  (exact conversion)
  │
  ▼
for band = 1 … 24 in index order, active bands only:
  │   Stereo : L ← F(L)        R ← F(R)        (two lanes, shared parameters)
  │   Left   : L ← F(L)        R untouched
  │   Right  : R ← F(R)        L untouched
  │   Mid    : m = 0.5 (L + R)   d = F(m) − m    L += d    R += d
  │   Side   : s = 0.5 (L − R)   d = F(s) − s    L += d    R −= d
  │   F = slot A, or  wA·slotA + wB·slotB  during a structural crossfade
  │   (mono layout: every band runs on the single channel)
  ▼
Listen path (if listenBand ≥ 0): crossfade to listen filter of the input
  ▼
Auto gain (ramped)  ← auto_gain, all bands
  ▼
Output gain (ramped)  ← output_gain
  ▼
Global soft bypass: crossfade processed ↔ dry input  ← bypass (host bypass parameter)
  ▼
double → float
  │
  ├──► Spectrum tap POST
  ├──► Output peak meter (atomics)
  ▼
Output
```

**Routing notes:**
- Strictly serial, no feedback, no parallel band split. Latency 0 samples in every configuration; `setLatencySamples(0)` in `prepareToPlay` (JUCE 8 `getLatencySamples()` is non-virtual).
- Inactive means: not enabled, or bypassed, or asleep (gain-bearing type whose effective gain has been exactly 0 dB for 50 ms), and no fade in progress. Inactive bands are not in the active list and cost nothing.
- The dry copy for the global bypass crossfade is taken only while a bypass fade is running. When fully bypassed the buffer is not touched and all filter state is cleared.
- `processBlockBypassed` is overridden and routed to the same soft-bypass engine so a host that ignores the bypass parameter still gets the click-free path.
- Bus layouts: mono→mono and stereo→stereo only. `(2,1)` and `(1,2)` are refused in `isBusesLayoutSupported` (suite lesson: buffer width is a max over inputs and outputs and says nothing about which channels are outputs). The stereo decision is a flag derived in `prepareToPlay` from the negotiated output set, not from `buffer.getNumChannels()`.

## System Architecture

### File I/O System
Not applicable. Presets are handled by the `preset-manager` module on the message thread.

### Multi-Output Routing
Not applicable. One input bus, one output bus. No sidechain bus in v1 (see Dynamic-EQ forward compatibility for the later sidechain).

### MIDI Routing
Not applicable. `acceptsMidi() == false`, `producesMidi() == false`.

### State Persistence

**What state is saved:**
- All 196 APVTS parameters (automatic).
- UI state in a `UI` child of the state tree: `analyzerMode` (0 Off, 1 Pre, 2 Post, 3 Pre+Post; default 2), `selectedBand`, editor size, language. Not part of presets.
- Root attributes `stateVersion="1"` and `pluginVersion`.

**Serialization format:** `AudioProcessorValueTreeState::copyState()` → XML → `copyXmlToBinary`. Presets: `preset-manager` 1.1.1 JSON keyed by parameter ID.

**Restore behaviour:**
- Missing parameter → its default. Unknown parameter or child → ignored. This is what makes a later version's session load in v1 and a v1 session load later.
- Invalid XML → defaults, no throw.
- `setStateInformation` never writes one parameter from another parameter's listener (VST3 swallows nested host notifications; suite lesson).
- Values read back from XML are parsed by type, never compared as strings (a bool round-trips as a string in ValueTree XML; suite lesson).
- Preset apply resets all parameters to defaults first, then applies the preset (suite lesson), so a preset that defines 3 bands switches the other 21 off.

**Dynamic-EQ forward compatibility (DSP-07):**

| Guarantee | Mechanism |
|-----------|-----------|
| v1 automation survives in VST3 | JUCE derives the VST3 `ParamID` from the hash of the parameter ID string (`JUCE_FORCE_USE_LEGACY_PARAM_IDS` is off suite-wide), so it does not depend on registration order. v1 IDs are frozen: never renamed, never removed, ranges and skews never changed. |
| v1 automation survives in AU (Logic, GarageBand index-based lookup) | JUCE sorts AUv2 parameters by version hint first, then by ID hash (`juce_AudioProcessorParameter.h`, 8.0.15). v1 uses hint 1. Dynamic-EQ parameters are added with hint 2, so they sort after every v1 parameter and no v1 index moves. |
| v1 sessions sound the same later | New parameters default to the static behaviour (`dyn_range` 0 dB). A state without them loads them at defaults. |
| The range of the reserved parameters is not frozen prematurely | They are not registered in v1. Registering them now would fix ranges that the dynamic-EQ design has not chosen, and a later range change would shift normalised automation. |
| Engine room | `Band::dynOffsetDb` is summed into the effective gain at each control tick (16 samples at 48 kHz). A detector only has to write that value. |

Reserved, not registered in v1: `bNN_dyn_range`, `bNN_dyn_threshold`, `bNN_dyn_auto` (NN = 01 … 24), version hint 2. Adding a sidechain input bus later is a bus-layout change that is optional and disabled by default; it does not affect parameter compatibility.

A Stage 1 gate freezes the layout: `tests/golden/params.tsv` (ID, index, version hint, range, skew, default, automatable) from the suite `param-dump` tool, diffed on every build.

## Parameter Mapping

**196 host parameters in v1** (192 band + 4 global). `analyzer` from the draft becomes UI state (see Open Question 4). All use `juce::ParameterID { id, 1 }`. No lambda `NormalisableRange` anywhere. Float ranges use interval 0 where an exact value matters.

**Registration order** (the order VST3 hosts list): group `global`, then groups `band01` … `band24` (`juce::AudioProcessorParameterGroup`, which JUCE maps to AU clumps so Logic shows one submenu per band). Inside a band: enabled, bypass, type, freq, gain, q, slope, placement.

### Global (4)

| Parameter ID | Type | Range / choices | Default | Skew | DSP Component | Usage |
|--------------|------|-----------------|---------|------|---------------|-------|
| `bypass` | Bool | Off / On | Off | — | Output Stage | Returned by `getBypassParameter()`. 20 ms crossfade to dry. |
| `output_gain` | Float, interval 0 | -36 … +36 dB | 0 | linear | Output Stage | Linear gain `10^(dB/20)`, 20 ms ramp. |
| `gain_scale` | Float, interval 0 | 0 … 200 % | 100 | linear | Prototype Builder | `gEff = gain * scale / 100`. 100 is exactly normalised 0.5. |
| `auto_gain` | Bool | Off / On | Off | — | Auto Gain | Enables the curve-derived compensation. |

### Per band (8 x 24 = 192), IDs `b01_…` to `b24_…`

| Parameter ID | Type | Range / choices | Default | Skew | DSP Component | Usage |
|--------------|------|-----------------|---------|------|---------------|-------|
| `bNN_enabled` | Bool | Off / On | Off | — | Band Runtime | Band exists. Automatable. Crossfaded. |
| `bNN_bypass` | Bool | Off / On | Off | — | Band Runtime | Band muted but kept. Crossfaded. |
| `bNN_type` | Choice (8) | Bell, Low Shelf, High Shelf, Low Cut, High Cut, Notch, Band Pass, Tilt Shelf | 0 Bell | — | Prototype Builder | Structural. Crossfaded. |
| `bNN_freq` | Float, interval 0 | 10 … 30000 Hz | 1000 | `setSkewForCentre(1000)`, skew 0.203214 | Prototype Builder | Centre / corner. Design frequency policy near Nyquist below. |
| `bNN_gain` | Float, interval 0 | -30 … +30 dB | 0 | linear | Prototype Builder | Bell, shelves, tilt. Ignored by cuts, notch, band pass. |
| `bNN_q` | Float, interval 0 | 0.025 … 40 | 1.0 | `setSkewForCentre(1.0)`, skew 0.186652 | Prototype Builder | Bell / Notch / Band Pass: bandwidth. Cuts / shelves / tilt: resonance factor. |
| `bNN_slope` | Choice (8) | 6, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96 dB/oct | 1 (12) | — | Prototype Builder | Order N = slope / 6. Inert for Bell, Notch, Band Pass. Inert Q at 6 dB/oct. |
| `bNN_placement` | Choice (5) | Stereo, Left, Right, Mid, Side | 0 Stereo | — | Router | Structural. Crossfaded. Inert on mono. |

Skew values: `skew = ln 0.5 / ln((centre − start) / (end − start))`. Frequency: `ln 0.5 / ln(990 / 29990)`. Q: `ln 0.5 / ln(0.975 / 39.975)`. With a pow skew the default 1 kHz sits at normalised 0.5; normalised 0.25 is 42.7 Hz and 0.75 is 7.29 kHz (a true log map would give 74 Hz and 4.05 kHz). The page draws on a true log axis from `getScaledValue()` and writes through `setNormalisedValue(((hz − 10) / 29990)^skew)`; the skew reaches the WebView frontend, a lambda range would not.

Host-visible names: `B1 On`, `B1 Bypass`, `B1 Type`, `B1 Freq`, `B1 Gain`, `B1 Q`, `B1 Slope`, `B1 Placement` … `B24 …`; `Bypass`, `Output Gain`, `Gain Scale`, `Auto Gain`.

### Answers to the six open questions in `parameter-spec-draft.md`

1. **Dynamic-EQ reservation.** Do not register the 72 parameters in v1. Reserve the IDs and version hint 2. Rationale and guarantees: State Persistence table above.
2. **Parameter order.** Global block first, then band-major. A VST3 host lists by registration order, so the four globals stay at the top instead of after 192 entries, and one band's eight parameters stay together. AU order inside a version hint is decided by JUCE's ID hash and cannot be chosen; the parameter groups keep it readable.
3. **`bNN_slope` on types that ignore it.** Honoured by Low Cut, High Cut, Low Shelf, High Shelf, Tilt Shelf. Inert for Bell, Notch, Band Pass: the value is stored, the DSP ignores it, the UI disables the control for those types. If a later version enables slope for those types it must gate on `stateVersion` and migrate v1 states to 12 dB/oct for those bands so v1 sessions do not change.
4. **`analyzer` and `bNN_enabled`.** Analyzer mode is UI state in the session, not a host parameter: it has no audio effect, it should not change on preset load, and it should not clutter the automation list or dirty the host's undo history. `bNN_enabled` is automatable: enable is click-free by construction and section-by-section automation needs it.
5. **Global `bypass`.** Yes. `getBypassParameter()` returns it; `processBlockBypassed` is also routed to the same engine.
6. **Frequency skew.** `NormalisableRange<float> (10, 30000, 0)` with `setSkewForCentre (1000)`. Q the same way with centre 1.0.

## Algorithm Details

Notation: `fs` sample rate, `fN = fs / 2`, `w = 2 π f / fs` rad/sample (may exceed π), `X(w, g) = tan²(w/2) / g²`.

### MatchedPair (the one primitive)

Maps an analog pair `s² + (w/Q) s + w²` to a digital pair by impulse invariance, `z = e^s` [PAPER: Vicanek 2016, eq. 11-12], with the pole angle clamped at π so a pair above Nyquist does not alias back into the band (Stage 0 addition).

```
MatchedPair(w, Q):                         # Q may be +inf (q = 0)
  q = 1 / (2Q)
  if q < 1:
      r  = exp(-q w)
      th = min( w * sqrt(1 - q²), π )
      s2 = sin²(th / 2)
      P0 = expm1(-q w)² + 4 r s2           # = 1 + a1 + a2
      P1 = (1 + r)² - 4 r s2               # = 1 - a1 + a2
  else:
      d  = w * sqrt(q² - 1)
      e1 = -expm1(-q w + d);  e2 = -expm1(-q w - d)     # 1 - p1, 1 - p2
      P0 = e1 e2
      P1 = (2 - e1)(2 - e2)
  Om = -expm1(-2 q w)                      # = 1 - a2
  g  = sqrt(P0 / P1)
  k  = 2 Om / sqrt(P0 P1)
  f  = w / π
  hN = f² / sqrt( (1 - f²)² + f² / Q² )    # analog 2-pole low-pass magnitude at Nyquist
  return P0, P1, Om, g, k, hN
```

`a1 = -2 r cos th`, `a2 = r²` are never formed. Derivation of `(g, k)`: the trapezoidal SVF denominator is the bilinear image of `s² + k s + 1` at `s = (z − 1) / (g (z + 1))`, giving `a1 = 2(g² − 1) / (1 + kg + g²)`, `a2 = (1 − kg + g²) / (1 + kg + g²)`, hence `g² = P0 / P1` and `k = 2(1 − a2) / sqrt(P0 P1)`. The stability triangle `P0 > 0, P1 > 0, a2 < 1` is exactly `g > 0, k > 0`.

Why the `expm1` forms: at 10 Hz and 192 kHz `P0 ≈ 1e-7`, so forming `1 + a1 + a2` from `a1 ≈ -2`, `a2 ≈ 1` loses about nine digits. A Stage 0 trial variant that formed such differences directly was wrong by more than 10 dB for 10 Hz bells with Q ≥ 10 at 44.1 kHz [MODEL]. With the forms above, the 10 Hz, Q 40, +30 dB bell at 192 kHz matches the analog prototype within 4e-13 dB [MODEL].

Guard: `P1 ≥ 1e-12`. It can only approach 0 for `q → 0` with `th = π`, which the notch frequency clamp prevents.

### SVF section and one-pole (realisation)

```
SVF, per sample (double state ic1, ic2):
  a1 = 1 / (1 + g (g + k));  a2 = g a1;  a3 = g a2      # recomputed per sample only while ramping
  v3 = x - ic2
  v1 = a1 ic1 + a2 v3
  v2 = ic2 + a2 ic1 + a3 v3
  ic1 = 2 v1 - ic1;  ic2 = 2 v2 - ic2
  y  = mL v2 + mB v1 + mH (x - k v1 - v2)

  response:  H = (mL + mB σ + mH σ²) / (1 + k σ + σ²),   σ = j tan(w/2) / g
             |H|² = ((mL - mH X)² + mB² X) / ((1 - X)² + k² X),   X = tan²(w/2) / g²

One-pole TPT, per sample (double state s):
  v = (x - s) G / (1 + G);  lp = v + s;  s = lp + v
  y = cL lp + cH (x - lp)

  response:  H = (cL + cH σ) / (1 + σ),   σ = j tan(w/2) / G
             |H|² = (cL² + cH² X) / (1 + X),   X = tan²(w/2) / G²
```

`mL` is the DC gain and `mH` the Nyquist gain of the section. Any biquad `b0..a2` with stable poles maps to this form by `mL = (b0+b1+b2)/P0`, `mH = (b0−b1+b2)/P1`, `mB = 2(b0−b2)/sqrt(P0 P1)`; the designer never needs the `b` coefficients. The recurrences were run on an impulse in the model and agree with the closed-form magnitude to 1e-14 dB [MODEL].

### Gain-bearing section: matched low-pass ratio (MLR)

Used for every bell and every shelf / tilt second-order section, boost and cut alike.

Analog section, zeros `(wz, Qz)`, poles `(wp, Qp)`, scalar `c`:

```
Ha(s) = c (wp² / wz²) (s² + (wz/Qz) s + wz²) / (s² + (wp/Qp) s + wp²)        # DC gain c
```

Idea: write it as a ratio of two all-pole low-passes, `Ha = c · LP(wp, Qp) / LP(wz, Qz)`, and replace each by Vicanek's matched low-pass with DC and Nyquist gain matched [PAPER: Vicanek 2016, section 5.1: matched pair in the denominator, numerator `b0 + b1 z⁻¹` with `b0 + b1 = P0` and `b0 − b1 = P1·hN`]. The ratio is a biquad (matched zeros over matched poles) times a first-order pole/zero pair.

```
N = MatchedPair(wz, Qz);   D = MatchedPair(wp, Qp)

SVF:        g = D.g    k = D.k
            mL = N.P0 / D.P0
            mB = 2 N.Om / sqrt(D.P0 D.P1)
            mH = N.P1 / D.P1
Corrector:  G  = N.g² / N.hN
            cL = c · D.P0 / N.P0
            cH = c · (D.hN D.P1) / (N.hN N.P1)
```

Properties (all by construction):
- DC gain exactly `c`; Nyquist gain exactly `c · D.hN / N.hN`, the analog section's gain at Nyquist.
- Swapping N and D gives the exact reciprocal. A cut is therefore the exact inverse of the boost with the same settings, with no special case. Boost / cut symmetry is exact.
- At 0 dB (`N = D`): `mL = mH = 1`, `mB = k`, `cL = cH = 1`, the identity.
- Always feasible and always stable: `g, k, G > 0` for every input. No branch on Q, gain or frequency.
- Minimum phase: the zeros are a matched (stable) pair.

Status: the composition is a Stage 0 derivation from Vicanek's matched low-pass, not a published design. It is supported by the numerical model below and must be re-proved by gate G1.

### Per-type prototypes

`A = 10^(gEff/40)`, `Gl = 10^(gEff/20)`, `wc` corner / centre in rad/sample, `Qu` the user Q, `N` the order.

Butterworth section Qs for order N: `Qi = 1 / (2 sin((2i + 1) π / (2N)))`, `i = 0 … floor(N/2) − 1`; `Q0` is the highest. Resonance rule for cuts, shelves and tilt: `Q0 ← Q0 · Qu`. So `Qu = 1` is Butterworth at every slope, and the gain at the corner of a cut is `Qu / sqrt 2` at every slope (the product of the Butterworth section Qs is `1/sqrt 2` for even N, and 1 times the one-pole's `1/sqrt 2` for odd N). Q is inert at 6 dB/oct.

| Type | Order | Analog sections | Digital design |
|------|-------|-----------------|----------------|
| Bell | 2 (slope inert) | `wz = wp = wc`, `Qz = Qu / A`, `Qp = Qu · A`, `c = 1`. This is `(s² + s wc A/Qu + wc²) / (s² + s wc/(A Qu) + wc²)`, the RBJ / Vicanek eq. 42 peaking prototype: bandwidth independent of gain sign. | MLR |
| Low Shelf | N | `r = Gl^(1/(2N))`. Each 2nd-order section: `wz = wc r`, `wp = wc / r`, `Qz = Qp = Qi`, `c = Gl^(2/N)`. Odd N adds `(s + wc r) / (s + wc / r)`, DC gain `Gl^(1/N)`. At N = 2 this is exactly the RBJ shelf. | MLR per section; first-order: Vicanek 2019 |
| High Shelf | N | Mirror: `wz = wc / r`, `wp = wc r`, `c = 1` (HF gain `Gl^(2/N)` per section). | same |
| Tilt Shelf | N | High shelf of gain `gEff`, times the scalar `10^(-gEff/40)`: lows `-gEff/2`, highs `+gEff/2`, 0 dB at `wc`. | same; scalar folded into the last section's `cL, cH` |
| Low Cut | N | Butterworth high-pass sections `s² / (s² + (wc/Qi) s + wc²)`; odd N adds `s / (s + wc)`. | matched high-pass |
| High Cut | N | Butterworth low-pass sections; odd N adds `wc / (s + wc)`. | 3-point matched low-pass |
| Notch | 2 (slope inert) | `(s² + wc²) / (s² + (wc/Qu) s + wc²)` | MLR with `Qz = +inf` (zeros exactly on the unit circle at `wc`) |
| Band Pass | 2 (slope inert) | `(wc/Qu) s / (s² + (wc/Qu) s + wc²)`, unity at `wc` | exact-peak matched band-pass |

**3-point matched low-pass (High Cut sections).** Matched pair, then the SVF numerator matched at DC, at `wm = min(wc, 0.75 π)` and at Nyquist:

```
D = MatchedPair(wc, Q);   Xm = X(wm, D.g);   y = (wm / wc)²
Ta  = 1 / ((1 - y)² + y / Q²)                      # analog |H|² at wm
mL  = 1;   mH = D.hN
mB² = ( Ta ((1 - Xm)² + D.k² Xm) - (1 - mH Xm)² ) / Xm ;   mB = sqrt(max(mB², 0))
```
`mB² < 0` did not occur on the model grid (fc 10 Hz - 30 kHz, Q 0.1 - 10, N 1 - 16, 44.1 and 48 kHz) [MODEL]; the `max` keeps the map continuous if it ever does.

**Matched high-pass (Low Cut sections).** Double zero at DC so the stop-band slope is exactly 12 dB/oct per section [PAPER: Vicanek 2016, section 4.2], match point capped:

```
D = MatchedPair(wc, Q);   wm = min(wc, 0.9 π);   Xm = X(wm, D.g);   y = (wm / wc)²
Ta = y² / ((1 - y)² + y / Q²)
mL = 0;  mB = 0;  mH = sqrt( Ta ((1 - Xm)² + D.k² Xm) ) / Xm
```

**First-order cut sections.** TPT one-pole with the matched pole `e^(-wc)`: `G = tanh(wc / 2)`. Low-pass: `cL = 1`, `cH = 1 / sqrt(1 + (π/wc)²)`. High-pass: `cL = 0`, `cH = (π/wc) / sqrt(1 + (π/wc)²)`. (DC and Nyquist gain equal to the analog one-pole.)

**First-order shelf section** [PAPER: Vicanek 2019, eq. 10-12, `fm = 0.9`]. High shelf `H(s) = (1 + sqrt(G) s) / (1 + s / sqrt(G))`, `s = j f / fc`, `fc` in units of Nyquist:

```
phm   = 1 - cos(π fm)
alpha = (2/π²)(1/fm² + 1/(G fc²)) - 1/phm
beta  = (2/π²)(1/fm² + G/fc²)     - 1/phm
a1 = -alpha / (1 + alpha + sqrt(1 + 2 alpha))
b  = -beta  / (1 + beta  + sqrt(1 + 2 beta))
b0 = (1 + a1) / (1 + b);   b1 = b b0
→ one-pole:  G1 = (1 + a1) / (1 - a1),  cL = (b0 + b1) / (1 + a1) = 1,  cH = (b0 - b1) / (1 - a1)
```
Low shelf of gain G = high shelf of gain 1/G scaled by G. For the odd-order section of an order-N shelf use the section's own gain `Gl^(1/N)` and corner `wc`. Valid for `fc` above Nyquist [PAPER]; boost and cut are mirror images [MODEL].

**Exact-peak matched band-pass.** Vicanek 2016 section 4.3 conditions (single zero at DC, unity gain at `wc`, maximum at `wc`), solved in SVF variables (Stage 0 derivation; it removes the cancellation in the paper's `B2`):

```
D = MatchedPair(wc, Q);   X0 = X(wc, D.g)
mL = 0
mH = sqrt(max(1 - 1/X0², 0))
mB = sqrt(max(D.k² + 2 (1 - X0) / X0, 0))
```

### Frequency policy near and above Nyquist

The parameter runs to 30 kHz; Nyquist is 22.05 kHz at 44.1 kHz. Nothing is ever handed a frequency that makes it unstable: every design above is stable for any `w > 0`. What changes is accuracy, so each type has a rule.

| Type | Rule | Model result at 44.1 kHz for 20 kHz < fc ≤ 30 kHz |
|------|------|------|
| High Cut, Low Cut | Design at the true frequency (pole / zero angles clamp at π). | 12 dB/oct high cut, Q 1: ≤ 0.57 dB down to -80 dB. |
| Shelves, Tilt (amended 2026-11-13, second amendment) | Per pair `(w0, Q)` (zeros, poles) of each second-order section with `w0 > wL = 0.95 π` and `Q > 1.5`: design the pair at `wT = w0 (wL / w0)^β` with `Qe = 1 / sqrt((1 − x²)² + x² / Q²)`, `x = wT / w0`, clamp to [0.025, 160]; `β = sstep((ln Q − ln 1.5) / (ln 4 − ln 1.5))`. The pair keeps its DC value and its magnitude at `wT`. Continuous at `w0 = wL` and at `Q = 1.5`. A pair with `w0 ≤ wL` or `Q ≤ 1.5` is designed at the true frequency, bit-unchanged from Phase 2.1. The first-order section is not re-centred. The polish target stays the true section. | 12 dB/oct Butterworth shelf (unchanged): ≤ 0.43 / 0.78 / 1.22 dB at ±6 / ±12 / ±30 dB. Sections with Q ≥ 4 and the upper pair above 0.9 Nyquist, closed form alone [BENCH]: mean 6.81 → 2.15 dB at 44.1 kHz and 5.51 → 2.21 dB at 48 kHz, worst 16.6 → 3.9 and 12.2 → 3.8 dB. |
| Bell | For `wc > wL = 0.95 π`: re-centre. Design a bell at `wL` whose gain is the true prototype's gain at `wL` and whose Q makes it also hit the true prototype at `wL / 2`. Closed form: `Ge = |Ha(wL)|`, `T = |Ha(wL/2)|²`, `Qe = sqrt( 0.25 (Ge − T/Ge) / (0.5625 (T − 1)) )` (fall back to `Qu` when numerator or denominator is ≤ 0, clamp to [0.025, 160]). Continuous at `wL`. | ≤ 0.95 / 1.72 / 2.70 dB at ±6 / ±12 / ±30 dB |
| Notch | `wc ← min(wc, 0.95 π)`. A notch above that has almost no in-band effect unless Q is very low. | Finite. The clamp parks the notch at 20.95 kHz: against the true above-Nyquist prototype, up to 13.6 dB (clamp - 25 kHz) and 18.9 dB (25 - 30 kHz) below 20 kHz [MODEL, Stage 2 research Q2]. Reported by G1, not gated. |
| Band Pass | `wc ← min(wc, 0.9 π)` | Finite. The peak is parked at 19.85 kHz: up to 25.4 dB (clamp - 25 kHz; 2.5 dB for Q ≤ 0.3) and 30.6 dB (25 - 30 kHz) against the true prototype [MODEL, Stage 2 research Q2]. Reported by G1, not gated. |

Sessions therefore translate across sample rates for bells, shelves and cuts: a 25 kHz bell made at 96 kHz still produces only its lower skirt at 44.1 kHz instead of a peak parked below Nyquist.

Maximum |digital − analog| in dB, 10 Hz - 20 kHz, worst case over Q and frequency in the zone [MODEL]. Cuts mirror boosts exactly.

| Design | fs | Zone | ±6 dB | ±12 dB | ±30 dB |
|--------|----|------|-------|--------|--------|
| Bell (MLR), Q 0.025 - 40 | 44.1 k | fc ≤ 16 k | 0.32 | 0.58 | 0.92 |
| Bell (MLR) | 44.1 k | 16 k < fc ≤ 20 k | 0.36 | 0.66 | 1.05 |
| Bell (MLR) | 48 k | fc ≤ 20 k | 0.22 | 0.39 | 0.58 |
| Bell (MLR) | 96 k | fc ≤ 20 k | 0.06 | 0.10 | 0.14 |
| Shelf 12 dB/oct, Q 1.0 (Butterworth) | 44.1 k | fc ≤ 10 k | 0.05 | 0.12 | 0.60 |
| Shelf 12 dB/oct, Q 1.0 | 44.1 k | 10 k < fc ≤ 20 k | 0.37 | 0.69 | 1.19 |
| Shelf 12 dB/oct, Q 0.25 - 1.41 | 44.1 k | 10 k < fc ≤ 20 k | 0.66 | 1.17 | 1.49 |

| Reference: RBJ pre-warped bilinear bell | 44.1 k | fc ≤ 20 k | — | — | 13 - 17 |

The table above is the closed form (the seed). From Phase 2.1b the bell and second-order shelf sections are polished; their figures are under "Accuracy polish (v1, Phase 2.1b)".

Known weak spots of the closed form, reported by gate G1 as INFO rows in Phase 2.1 (from Phase 2.1b the steep-shelf row is binding and the resonant-shelf row stays INFO at the polished level):
- Resonant shelves (Q above 1.41) with the corner above 10 kHz at 44.1 / 48 kHz: the resonance sits at or beyond Nyquist; up to about 5 dB at ±6 dB, Q 10, fc 20 kHz. Below 10 kHz they are within 0.14 / 0.31 dB at ±6 / ±12 dB.
- Shelves of 24 dB/oct and steeper with the corner above 10 kHz at 44.1 kHz: section errors add (table row above).
- High cut skirts: 12 dB/oct within 1.1 dB down to -80 dB for fc ≤ 10 kHz. 48 and 96 dB/oct, measured in the top 30 dB: within 2.1 / 1.2 dB for fc ≤ 10 kHz and 3.6 / 5.7 dB for fc 10 - 20 kHz, which on those skirts is a frequency shift of under 0.1 octave. The corner itself is matched exactly.
- Low cut: Q 1.0, fc ≤ 10 kHz within 0.09 dB (12 dB/oct) and 0.00 dB (48, 96 dB/oct).
- Notch (fc ≤ 10 kHz: ≤ 0.63 dB where the prototype is above -40 dB; 10 - 20 kHz: ≤ 1.12 dB). Band pass (≤ 1.5 dB in the top 40 dB for fc ≤ 10 kHz at 44.1 kHz; weaker above; exact at the peak).

The display always shows the realised response (UI-02), so these deviations are visible, not hidden.

### Parameter smoothing and the control grid

- Global control grid of `K` samples, counted from the first sample after `prepareToPlay` and continuing across host blocks: `K = 16` for fs ≤ 48 kHz, 32 for ≤ 96 kHz, 64 for ≤ 192 kHz. Host block size never changes where the ticks fall, which makes renders block-size invariant.
- At each tick, for each active band whose ramp is not finished or whose `dynOffsetDb` changed: advance the ramps (log frequency, effective gain in dB, log Q; 20 ms linear, `round (0.020 fs / K)` ticks, arrival counted; `gain_scale` has no ramp of its own, it moves the effective gain `clamp (gain · scale / 100)` of each gain-bearing band, and `dynOffsetDb` is added after the ramp; amended 2026-11-13, Phase 2.3 plan), run Prototype + Designer, store the new section parameter sets as the tick target.
- Between ticks each section parameter (`g, k, mL, mB, mH, G, cL, cH`) moves linearly per sample from the previous set to the target. Linear interpolation between two points with `g, k, G > 0` stays positive, so every intermediate filter is a stable, realisable SVF. `a1, a2, a3` are recomputed per sample from the interpolated `g, k` (one division) on the ramping path only.
- Stability under time variation (updated 2026-11-13, RESEARCH-2.3 Q2): the trapezoidal SVF is BIBO stable under arbitrary per-sample variation of `g` and `k` inside a bounded box with `g, k > 0` (Wishnick, DAFx-14, proof read; this engine's box is `g` 2.9e-5 to 257, `k` 7.9e-4 to 1256). Shorter argument, derived and checked numerically: the state matrix `P` satisfies `I − PᵀP = (4gk / D²) v vᵀ`, `D = 1 + gk + g²`, `v = (1, −g)`, so with zero input the Euclidean norm of the state never grows. Both hold only if `a1, a2, a3` are computed each sample from one `(g, k)` pair; interpolating `a1, a2, a3` independently is outside the argument and is not used. Gate G5 tests it directly.
- Targets are sanitised before they reach a ramp: non-finite values are replaced by the parameter default, then clamped to range. A ramp's current value is set explicitly in `prepareToPlay` (`SmoothedValue::reset` keeps a NaN; suite lesson — the engine uses its own ramp type and never relies on reset to clear state).
- Settled bands take the constant-parameter path and do no design work.

### Structural changes: two-slot crossfade

Type, slope, placement, enabled and bypass change the section list or the lanes; a filter family switch on live state clicks whether or not the state is reset (suite lesson, measured 750x - 2000x on O-SimpleReverb). So structure never changes on a running chain.

- Each band has slots A and B. On a structural change the idle slot is configured with the new structure and placement, its state cleared, its parameters set to the current (not ramping-from-zero) values; both slots then run on the same band input for 20 ms and their contributions are mixed with raised-cosine weights `wB = 0.5 − 0.5 cos(π t / T)`, `wA = 1 − wB` (amplitude-complementary, since the two outputs are correlated).
- "Off" is a slot whose contribution is the dry band input (for Mid / Side: a zero difference). Enable, disable, bypass, un-bypass, wake and sleep are the same crossfade against that slot.
- A new structural request during a fade is latched (latest wins) and starts when the current fade ends.
- Neutral sleep: a Bell, shelf or tilt band whose ramped effective gain has been exactly 0 dB for 50 ms fades to "off" and leaves the active list; it wakes with a fade the moment the target moves. This is what makes "all bands at 0 dB" bit-transparent (QUAL-01) rather than merely close.
- After a fade the retired slot's state is cleared.

### Auto gain

Deterministic and program-independent, so null tests and offline renders are repeatable.

```
grid:   f_i, i = 0 … 63, log-spaced 40 Hz … min(16 kHz, 0.45 fs); equal weights (pink-noise assumption)
band b: p_b[i] = Σ over its sections of ln |H_section(f_i)|²        (target parameters, closed form)
lanes:  PL[i] = exp( Σ p_b[i] over active Stereo, Mid and Left bands )
        PR[i] = exp( Σ p_b[i] over active Stereo, Mid and Right bands )      # mono: all bands
AG_dB = -10 log10( mean_i( 0.5 (PL[i] + PR[i]) ) ),  clamped to [-18, +12] dB
```
- Models a centre-panned program: Side bands do not change it; Left / Right bands count at half weight. Stated approximation.
- Only a band whose target changed recomputes its `p_b`; the sum is refreshed at most every 1024 samples at 48 kHz (scaled with fs) on the control grid, on the audio thread. No message-thread round trip, so offline renders match real-time ones.
- The gain ramps 100 ms. With `auto_gain` off the gain is exactly 1.0 and the stage is skipped.
- The +12 dB cap follows the suite lesson that an uncapped auto gain boost is a hazard.

Rejected: measured loudness matching (input vs output RMS / LUFS). It depends on the programme, pumps on transients, and breaks null tests.

### True-response display

- `DisplayModel` on the message thread reads the 196 parameter values and the sample rate (atomics), runs Prototype + Designer for each enabled band with the target values, and sends per-band packets `{ band, type, placement, active, sections: [[g, k, mL, mB, mH] …], onePoles: [[G, cL, cH] …] }` through `emitEventIfBrowserIsVisible ("eqSections", …)`. Only bands whose parameters changed are sent; a full push happens when the page asks at init (pull, not a one-shot push; suite lesson) and after preset load.
- The page evaluates the complex section responses from the closed forms in "SVF section and one-pole" at pixel resolution, and composes bands as 2x2 matrices in L/R: Stereo `F·I`; Left `diag(F, 1)`; Right `diag(1, F)`; Mid `I + (F − 1)·½[[1,1],[1,1]]`; Side `I + (F − 1)·½[[1,−1],[−1,1]]`. The drawn sums are the diagonal terms the mockup chooses (LL / RR or MM / SS); all four are exact.
- Why this is the true response: the display runs the same designer code as the audio thread on the same parameter values and the same sample rate. It shows the target, which the audio reaches within one 20 ms ramp. It does not depend on `processBlock` running, so it is correct with the transport stopped (suite lesson: state published only from `processBlock` goes stale when the host idles the audio thread).
- No lock, no FIFO and no audio-thread work is needed for the curve.
- Rejected: C++ pushes sampled curves (24 bands x 512 points at 30-60 Hz while dragging, and a fixed resolution); JS re-implements the designer (two implementations of the design maths drift; with section parameters pushed, JS only holds two three-line response formulas, covered by gate G9).

### Analyzer

- Audio thread: when the editor is open and the mode needs it, write the mono sum `0.5 (L + R)` (or the single channel) of the input block and of the output block into two single-producer / single-consumer rings (`juce::AbstractFifo`, 32768 floats each, allocated in `prepareToPlay`). If a ring is full the block is dropped. No FFT, no lock, no allocation.
- Message thread, 30 Hz editor timer: drain the rings into a sliding window; FFT size 4096 for fs ≤ 48 kHz, 8192 for ≤ 96 kHz, 16384 for ≤ 192 kHz (bin spacing about 11.7 Hz at every rate); Hann window; `performFrequencyOnlyForwardTransform` on a scratch copy (it overwrites its buffer in place); power → dB; per-bin release ballistics 20 dB/s, instant attack; reduce to 256 log-spaced display points (maximum within each point's span); emit `analyzerPre` / `analyzerPost` float arrays.
- Mode Off stops the audio-thread writes.

---

## Integration Points

### Feature Dependencies
- Designer → Section Engine: the engine only ever receives parameter sets from the designer.
- Band Runtime → Router: a slot carries its own placement, so a placement change is a slot change.
- Auto Gain → Designer output: it evaluates the same section parameter sets.
- Display Model → Prototype + Designer: same code, second instance.
- Listen → Designer + Section Engine.
- Analyzer taps → nothing in the audio path depends on them.

### Parameter Interactions
- `gain_scale` multiplies every gain-bearing band's dB gain; it is ramped like a band gain. At 0 % every such band reaches exactly 0 dB and goes to sleep, so the response is flat and bit-transparent once the fades end.
- `bNN_gain` is ignored by cuts, notch and band pass. `bNN_slope` is ignored by bell, notch and band pass. `bNN_q` is ignored at 6 dB/oct. Ignored means: the value is stored and shown disabled; changing it triggers no design work and no fade.
- `bNN_enabled` off wins over `bNN_bypass`.
- No parameter writes another parameter. Creating a band from the UI sets that band's parameters from the page inside one gesture group.
- `bypass` on: after the fade the engine is idle; parameter changes made while bypassed take effect on un-bypass because targets are read from the APVTS atomics at the next processed block, not cached from the last one (suite lesson on engine state synced only in `processBlock`).

### Processing Order Requirements
1. Pre tap before anything else (true input spectrum).
2. Bands in index order. Order matters only when L/R and M/S bands are mixed (the 2x2 matrices do not commute); index order is the definition and the display composes in the same order.
3. Listen crossfade after the band chain, before gains.
4. Auto gain, then output gain: output gain stays an absolute trim.
5. Global bypass crossfade last, against the untouched input.
6. Post tap and meter after the bypass stage (what the listener hears).

### Thread Boundaries

**Audio thread:** everything in the Processing Chain, the control-grid design step, auto gain estimation, ring writes. Reads parameters through `getRawParameterValue()->load()`. No allocation, no lock, no message-thread call.

**Message thread:** editor, WebView relays, Display Model (its own designer instance and scratch), FFT and analyzer smoothing, preset manager, UI state.

**No background thread.**

**Communication:**
- Parameters: APVTS atomics.
- UI state to audio: `std::atomic<int> listenBand`, `std::atomic<int> analyzerMode`, `std::atomic<bool> editorOpen`.
- Audio to UI: two `AbstractFifo` rings; `std::atomic<float>` output peaks (L, R) with peak-hold read-and-reset; `std::atomic<double> sampleRate`.
- The curve needs no channel in either direction.

---

## Implementation Risks

### Matched Section Designer (MLR)
**Complexity:** HIGH. **Risk Level:** MEDIUM-HIGH.

**Risk factors:**
- The gain-section design is a Stage 0 composition verified only in a float64 model.
- Accuracy degrades for resonant shelves and steep shelves near Nyquist (documented INFO rows).
- Low-frequency numerics depend on the cancellation-free forms.

**Alternative approaches considered and measured** [MODEL, 44.1 kHz, fc ≤ 20 kHz unless noted]:
1. Vicanek 2016 section 4.4 bell (boost side, inverted for cuts): 0.79 / 1.44 / 2.56 dB at ±6 / ±12 / ±30. Used alone it has no shelf design for Q other than Butterworth.
2. Orfanidis 1997 prescribed-Nyquist-gain bell (as restated in Vicanek 2016 eq. 13-16): not better where valid (0.74 dB at +6 dB, 10 kHz, Q 0.71) and undefined when the bandwidth reaches Nyquist.
3. Matched-Z with DC normalisation only: up to 3 dB at ±6 dB above 18 kHz.
4. Three-point numerator fit on matched poles (DC, centre, Nyquist): infeasible (negative `mB²`) for most cuts and for high shelves.
5. Five-point linear solve for all coefficients: infeasible stripes and 5 - 25 dB errors for in-band peaks.
6. Gauss-Newton polish of the five SVF parameters: reaches 2 - 5x lower error in two iterations where it converges, but diverged at low Q with a naive match grid. Not robust enough to adopt blind. (Amended 2026-11-13: Stage 2 research found the cause, a match grid with no points tied to the peak, and a robust form. See "Accuracy polish (v1, Phase 2.1b)".)
7. Massberg 2011: low-pass only; not evaluated numerically.
8. Oversampling: excluded by the brief (latency, and it is not needed).

**Fallback architecture:** if gate G1 fails in C++ for MLR, fall back to Vicanek 2016 section 4.4 for the bell (tolerance 0.15 + 0.14 |g|) and Vicanek 2024 two-pole Butterworth shelves with shelf Q inert; the SVF realisation, smoothing, crossfades and display are unchanged because the designer's output format is the same.

**Mitigation:** Phase 2.1 implements the designer alone with an offline gate harness before any processor code; the Stage 0 tables are its expected values.

### Click-free modulation and structural crossfades
**Complexity:** HIGH. **Risk Level:** MEDIUM.

**Risk factors:** time-varying behaviour is argued, not proved here; a 20 ms crossfade into a slow filter (10 Hz, Q 40) changes level over hundreds of milliseconds, which is correct but confounds a whole-window click metric.

**Alternatives:** coefficient interpolation on a direct-form biquad (not guaranteed stable between two stable sets, state meaning changes); resetting state on change (clicks); single chain with morphing section count (no continuous path between orders).

**Fallback:** lengthen the crossfade to 40 ms and the control ramp to 30 ms; drop per-sample parameter interpolation to every 4 samples only if CPU requires it.

**Mitigation:** gate G3 uses local κ (5 ms frames), a hard negative control (smoothing disabled must read ≥ 10x), and deep-side toggles rather than toggles around a neutral setting.

### Bit transparency with 24 serial bands
**Complexity:** MEDIUM. **Risk Level:** LOW-MEDIUM.

**Risk factors:** any always-on stage (a gain multiply by a ramp that ends at 0.99999994, a denormal offset, a dither) breaks `memcmp`. The Mid / Side path is exact only to rounding.

**Fallback:** none needed; the fast path is a branch.

**Mitigation:** gate G4 with `memcmp` at many block sizes; ramps snap to their target and report "settled".

### CPU at 24 x 96 dB/oct
**Complexity:** MEDIUM. **Risk Level:** MEDIUM.

**Risk factors:** the cost model is not a measurement; the ramping path adds a division per section per sample; 96 dB/oct shelves cost a corrector per section.

**Alternatives:** 2-wide SIMD over the L/R lanes of Stereo bands (`juce::dsp::SIMDRegister<double>`), which roughly halves Stereo-band cost.

**Fallback:** enable the lane-pair SIMD path in Stage 4 if the scalar budget is missed.

### WebView scale: 196 relays and a 60 Hz curve
**Complexity:** MEDIUM. **Risk Level:** MEDIUM.

**Risk factors:** 192 band relays (72 slider, 48 toggle, 72 combo) plus 4 global is more than any current suite plugin was checked for in this stage [UNVERIFIED]; editor open time and message traffic are unknown.

**Fallback:** bind only the selected band's eight parameters through relays and drive the other bands through two native functions (`getBandParams`, `setBandParam` with begin / end gesture). The parameter layout does not change.

**Mitigation:** measure editor open time and idle message rate in Phase 3.1 before building the curve.

### Overall Project Risk
**Overall complexity:** HIGH. **Highest risk component:** the Matched Section Designer (about half of the DSP risk), then click-free structure changes.

**Recommended approach:** designer and its gate first (2.1), static engine and transparency (2.2), continuous modulation (2.3), structural crossfades (2.4), output stage (2.5), analyzer / display model / listen (2.6).

## Architecture Decisions

### One designer, expressed in SVF parameters
**Decision:** every section is described by `(g, k, mL, mB, mH)` and optionally `(G, cL, cH)`; biquad `b0..a2` coefficients never exist in the plugin.
**Rationale:** it resolves the tension in the brief. Matched designs normally yield direct-form coefficients; the SVF is the modulation-safe structure; the map between them is a bijection on the stable set, and `mL`, `mH` are simply the DC and Nyquist gains. Interpolating in this domain is always stable, and the same five numbers drive the audio, the auto gain and the display.
**Alternatives:** TDF-II biquads with coefficient smoothing (rejected: suite measurements of family-switch and near-Nyquist explosions); JUCE `StateVariableTPTFilter` (rejected: bilinear cramping, three fixed outputs, float or double but no mix access).
**Tradeoffs:** one extra one-pole per gain-bearing section (about 0.4 of an SVF).

### Third-order gain sections (biquad plus corrector)
**Decision:** accept a first-order corrector per bell / shelf section.
**Rationale:** a single biquad cannot match both the resonance and the Nyquist end from a closed form; the corrector buys a 2 - 3x lower error than the best closed-form biquad and exact boost / cut symmetry.
**Tradeoffs:** CPU, and the response is no longer "a biquad", which only matters to the documentation.

### Slope applies to cuts, shelves and tilt only in v1
**Decision:** Bell, Notch and Band Pass stay second order.
**Rationale:** higher-order band shapes need the low-pass-to-band-pass pole transformation and produce sections with unequal zero and pole frequencies and Qs, where the model shows MLR is weakest near Nyquist. DSP-03's acceptance criteria are stated for the cuts. Getting 2nd-order bells right is the v1 quality bar.
**When to revisit:** v1.x, behind `stateVersion`, once the accuracy backlog (below) is addressed.
**Unverified premise:** that Pro-Q offers 6 - 96 dB/oct on every shape, and that its Q 1 on a cut is Butterworth [UNVERIFIED]; the Q 1.0 = Butterworth convention here was chosen on its own merits (default Q 1.0 gives a flat cut).

### Display designed on the message thread
**Decision:** see "True-response display".
**Tradeoff:** the curve shows the target, not the 20 ms ramp in flight.

### Dynamic-EQ parameters not registered in v1
**Decision and rationale:** State Persistence.
**Tradeoff:** a v1.x session opened in v1.0 loses the dynamic settings (they are ignored), which is the normal downgrade behaviour.

### Float I/O, double engine
**Decision:** `supportsDoublePrecisionProcessing()` returns false; the engine converts to double working buffers. Float → double → float is exact for untouched samples, except denormal ones: under `ScopedNoDenormals` a denormal float converts to 0.0. A lane that no active band touches is therefore never converted or written back (amended 2026-11-13, Phase 2.2 plan).
**Rationale:** one code path; the precision that matters is the filter state.

### Accuracy polish (v1, Phase 2.1b)

Replaces "Accuracy backlog (not v1)" (amended 2026-11-13; Stage 2 CONTEXT D7, `stages/2-dsp/RESEARCH-2.1.md`). Figures are [MODEL] from that research unless marked.

**Decision:** every MLR section of a Bell, Low Shelf, High Shelf or Tilt Shelf (the second-order gain sections) is refined by a fixed-iteration anchored Gauss-Newton fit toward the true analog section. Cuts, Notch, Band Pass and the first-order shelf section keep the closed form. The closed form is the seed and the fallback (D7c). No section is added: the fit uses the corrector one-pole that MLR already carries.

**What was found.** Stage 0's "best single biquad" reference (0.08 / 0.16 / 0.37 dB) does not extend to the full G1 grid, where a lone biquad is no better than MLR (0.24 / 0.54 / 1.40 dB). The shipped section is a biquad plus the corrector, and that third-order section can reach about 0.005 / 0.009 / 0.021 dB at ±6 / ±12 / ±30 dB at 44.1 kHz. The v1 polish reaches about 0.04 / 0.08 / 0.19 dB for bells and 0.04 / 0.12 / 0.19 dB for 12 dB/oct shelves with Q ≤ 1.41 (seed: 0.34 / 0.61 / 0.98 and 0.66 / 1.17 / 1.48).

**Algorithm** (the constants are part of the design; one header, both threads):

```
free:    φ = ln (g, k, mB, mH, G, cH)          mL and cL stay at the seed's values (DC gain exact)
target:  the TRUE analog section (wz, Qz, wp, Qp, c), also for a bell whose seed is re-centred
grid:    26 points: 16 fixed, log-spaced 20 Hz … min(20 kHz, 0.499 fs)   (tan² constants per rate)
         + 10 tied: for each of (wz, Qz) and (wp, Qp): w0, and w0 (sqrt(1 + h²) ± h), h = s / (2Q), s = 0.5, 1.5
         all clamped into 20 Hz … min(20 kHz, 0.499 fs)
r_j   =  (10 / ln 10) (ln |H(w_j)|² − ln |Ha(w_j)|²)                     dB
step:    A = JᵀJ + (λ diag(JᵀJ) + μ) I,   b = Jᵀr + μ (φ − φ0),   φ ← φ − A⁻¹ b      6x6 Cholesky
         λ = 1e-3,  μ = 0.1
limit:   δ = A⁻¹ b;  δ ← δ · R / sqrt(R² + |δ|²),  R = 0.35 (Euclidean norm over the six parameters); φ ← φ − δ
rate:    fs < 44.1 kHz: no polish at all; the design is the seed (decided once in Designer::prepare)
run:     S0 = Σ r² at the seed.  If S0 / 26 ≤ Sa²: keep the seed, exactly.      Sa = 0.002 dB
         K = 2 steps → φ2.  wx = sstep((rms(φ2) − Sx) / Sx),  Sx = 0.03 dB.
         If wx > 0: two more steps → φ4;  φ ← φ2 + wx (φ4 − φ2)
accept:  out = φ0 + a (φ − φ0),
         a = sstep((S0/26 − Sa²) / (Sb² − Sa²)) · sstep((1 − S1/S0) / 0.1),   Sb = 0.006 dB
         a = 0 for any non-finite value.     sstep = cubic smoothstep
cut:     design and polish the boost (gEff ≥ 0; for a shelf, Gl ≥ 1), then emit the exact inverse:
         g' = g sqrt(mL/mH)   k' = mB / sqrt(mL mH)   mL' = 1/mL   mB' = k / sqrt(mL mH)   mH' = 1/mH
         G' = G cL / cH       cL' = 1/cL              cH' = 1/cH
```

The Jacobian is closed form (RESEARCH-2.1 Q3). No step is accepted or rejected inside the loop and every decision is a weight, so the output is a continuous function of the inputs; a binary version of the same logic measured 0.06 - 0.13 dB jumps.

**Continuity (amended 2026-11-13, second amendment).** The first build diverged where a section has Q of about 4 or more and its upper pair is above about 0.9 Nyquist: the seed is 5 - 12 dB off there, four of the six parameters are nearly unobserved, and one undamped step moved `ln mB` by +19.5. The 26-point accept test does not see a resonance between its points. Two changes, both needed [BENCH]: the shelf re-centre on the seed side (the seed is then about 2 dB off, not 7) and the step limit above. Either one alone leaves jumps or steep spots. With both, at 44.1 / 48 kHz: 0 non-shrinking jumps on 5340 random lines (first build: 19 on 2700), 0 sections accepted with g or k more than 10x from the seed in 4.5 million (first build: 1072 / 662 per 2.25 million), worst excess over the seed off the gated grid +0.67 dB (first build +54). About 1 line in 1000 is still steeper than 2x the seed (2.4x at worst, continuous, shrinking with the step), which is why the gate's ratio limit is 4x and the shrink test is the binding one.

**Properties.** `g, k, G > 0` and positive numerator parameters by construction (log parameters): stable, minimum phase, invertible. Reciprocity holds to about 1e-12 dB. Allocation-free, bounded (2 or 4 steps), deterministic. No per-design sample-rate branch (the one rate decision is made in `prepare`: off below 44.1 kHz): where the seed is already within 0.002 dB RMS on the match grid the section keeps it (68 → 49 % of bell settings at 44.1 kHz from ±6 to ±30 dB; 79 - 94 % at 192 kHz).

**Results, polished** (max |err| dB, 20 Hz - 20 kHz, ±6 / ±12 / ±30 dB):

| Design | 44.1 k | 48 k | ≥ 88.2 k |
|--------|--------|------|----------|
| Bell, Q 0.025 - 40, fc ≤ 20 k | 0.043 / 0.081 / 0.193 | 0.016 / 0.026 / 0.073 | ≤ 0.013 |
| Shelf 12 dB/oct, Q ≤ 1.41 | 0.04 / 0.12 / 0.19 | ≤ 0.03 / 0.06 / 0.11 | ≤ 0.01 / 0.01 / 0.06 |
| Shelf 24 - 96 dB/oct, Q 1.0 | 0.06 / 0.12 / 0.23 | same bound as above | same bound as above |
| Shelf 18 dB/oct, Q 1.0 (odd order: the first-order section is not polished) | 0.06 / 0.15 / 0.28 | | |
| Bell, 20 k < fc ≤ 30 k (re-centred seed), random sweep to ±30 dB | 2.66 → 0.40 | 2.51 → 0.17 | |

**Known limits (INFO rows of G1 from Phase 2.1b):**
- Resonant shelves (Q above 1.41) with the corner above 10 kHz at 44.1 kHz (amended 2026-11-13, second amendment) [BENCH]: 12 dB/oct, Q 2 - 10: 0.18 / 0.44 / 0.45 dB at ±6 / ±12 / ±30 dB; Q 20 - 40: 0.75 / 1.03 / 0.43 dB. The formerly poor cell (Q 2 - 10, ±30 dB: 4.25 dB) is 0.45 dB with the re-centred seed. With the corner at 20 - 30 kHz, Q 2 - 40: 0.58 / 0.22 / 0.38 dB. Still INFO: the harness grid differs from the bench's.
- Odd-order shelves carry the unpolished Vicanek 2019 one-pole; the 6 dB/oct shelf is unchanged (0.17 / 0.31 / 0.49).
- Below 44.1 kHz (22.05, 32 kHz) there is no polish (amended 2026-11-13, second amendment): it was not reliably more accurate there and is not continuous there with or without the fix (the match band runs to 0.998 Nyquist, above the re-centre point). The design is the closed form, bit for bit. G5 covers stability.
- The objective is least squares on 26 points, not the gate's maximum error; that is the gap between 0.04 dB and the 0.005 dB optimum.
- Not modelled in research, measured by the Phase 2.1b harness: Tilt as its own type, 36 and 72 dB/oct shelves, 96 dB/oct shelves with user Q above 4.

**Cost.** Seed 30 - 36 ns per section, seed plus polish 0.77 - 0.90 µs per section (C++ research port, Apple M4 Max, scalar). See "Performance". The polish runs on every control tick while a band ramps (plan P2). The documented fallback if the Phase 2.2 smoke reading shows a problem is a correction hold: seed every tick, polish every fourth tick, and add the last log-domain correction `φ − φ0` to the new seed in between (untested).

## Special Considerations

### Thread Safety
- Parameter reads: `getRawParameterValue()->load()` once per block per parameter (392 loads worst case), structural values compared with the previous block's.
- Designer is reentrant; each thread has its own scratch.
- Rings: one writer (audio), one reader (message).
- No `AsyncUpdater` or `callAsync` in the audio path.

### Performance
Section counts, stereo, all 24 bands active:

| Configuration | SVF per sample | One-poles per sample |
|---------------|----------------|----------------------|
| 24 bells | 48 | 48 |
| 24 cuts at 96 dB/oct (PERF-02 case) | 384 | 0 |
| 24 shelves at 96 dB/oct | 384 | 384 |

Cost model [TARGET]: settled SVF about 8 multiplies and 11 adds, serially dependent, 2.5 ns per sample on a current desktop core; one-pole about 1 ns.

| Case, 48 kHz stereo | Model | Budget |
|---------------------|-------|--------|
| 24 cuts x 96 dB/oct, settled | 384 x 2.5 ns = 0.96 µs/sample = 4.6 % of a core | **≤ 10 % of one core** (PERF-02) |
| 24 shelves x 96 dB/oct, settled | 1.34 µs/sample = 6.5 % | ≤ 14 % |
| Same as PERF-02 case with all 24 bands sweeping (design ≤ 2 µs per 8-section band per tick x 3000 ticks/s = 14 %, settled cost 4.6 %, one division per section per sample about 3 %) | about 22 % | ≤ 35 % |
| 0 bands enabled | buffer untouched | ≤ 0.3 % and ≤ 1.5x a pass-through harness |

Amended 2026-11-13, measured design cost (C++ research port, Apple M4 Max, scalar): the seed is 30 - 36 ns per section, so the "≤ 2 µs per 8-section band" line above is about 7x pessimistic for cuts (which are never polished; the PERF-02 rows are unaffected). A polished section costs 0.77 - 0.90 µs. Design cost with every band sweeping at 3000 ticks/s and every section polished on every tick:

| Case | Polished sections | Design cost |
|------|-------------------|-------------|
| 24 bells, or 24 shelves x 12 dB/oct | 24 | 5.8 % of a core |
| 24 shelves x 48 dB/oct | 96 | 23 % |
| 24 shelves x 96 dB/oct | 192 | 46 % (INFO row of G10; not a PERF-02 case) |

Gate G10 measures on the development machine in Release at 512-sample blocks and also checks a ratio that is machine-independent: cost(24 bands) ≤ 24 x cost(1 band) x 1.15.

SIMD: deferred. The model meets the budget in scalar code, and the serial band order offers no cross-band vectorisation. Data layout keeps a Stereo band's two lanes adjacent with shared parameters so the 2-wide path can be added without restructuring.

### Denormal Protection
`juce::ScopedNoDenormals` at the top of `processBlock`. No DC offset injection (it would break bit transparency). Ring-down of a 10 Hz, Q 40 band is physical: `8.686 π f / Q_pole` dB/s, with `Q_pole = Q · 10^(gain / 40)` on a boost, so 3.42 dB/s at +12 dB and 6.8 dB/s only at 0 dB (corrected 2026-11-13, RESEARCH-2.3 Q3); with flush-to-zero it reaches exact zero.

### Sample Rate Handling
- 44.1 - 192 kHz supported; the engine is stable at any rate (pluginval and some hosts use 22.05 and 32 kHz; G5 covers them).
- `prepareToPlay`: store fs, choose `K`, size working buffers for the host's maximum block and for larger blocks (the engine processes oversized host blocks in chunks of the prepared size; suite lesson), allocate rings and FFT, clear all state, set ramps to their targets, `setLatencySamples (0)`.
- All designs are functions of `w = 2 π f / fs`; nothing is cached across a rate change.
- `getTailLengthSeconds()` returns 2.0.

### Latency
0 samples, always. No look-ahead, no oversampling, no FIR. Minimum phase: every section has its poles and zeros inside the unit circle.

## Research References

### Papers and notes (read in full unless marked)
- Vicanek, M., "Matched Second Order Digital Filters", 14 February 2016. https://www.vicanek.de/articles/BiquadFits.pdf — impulse-invariant poles (eq. 12), `φ` form of the magnitude (eq. 25-27), matched LP / HP / BP / peaking (sections 4.1-4.4), simpler DC-and-Nyquist fits (section 5). Basis of this design.
- Vicanek, M., "Matched One-Pole Digital Shelving Filters", 7 September 2019, revised 24 September 2019. https://www.vicanek.de/articles/ShelvingFits.pdf — first-order shelf, valid for corners above Nyquist. Used as is; re-verified in the model.
- Vicanek, M., "Matched Two-Pole Digital Shelving Filters", 23 March 2024, revised 10 December 2025. https://www.vicanek.de/articles/2poleShelvingFits.pdf — Butterworth-only two-pole shelf; the documented fallback. Its "never exceeds 1 dB for a 20 dB shelf" was not re-measured [UNVERIFIED].
- Orfanidis, S. J., "Digital Parametric Equalizer Design With Prescribed Nyquist-Frequency Gain", JAES 45(6), 444-455, June 1997. Evaluated from the restatement in Vicanek 2016 eq. 13-16; the original was not read.
- Massberg, M., "Digital Low-Pass Filter Design with Analog-Matched Magnitude Response", AES Convention 131, October 2011 (AES e-library 16077, as cited by Vicanek 2016; the repo research doc gives convention paper 8416, not checked) [UNVERIFIED]. Known only through Vicanek's restatement (eq. 20-23); low-pass only; not evaluated numerically.
- Wishnick, A., "Time-Varying Filters for Musical Applications", DAFx-14, Erlangen, 2014. https://dafx.de/paper-archive/details/yfd4LbdXr2Cywsqxfby8ug — abstract only: proposes the SVF and gives a proof of its stable time-varying behaviour [UNVERIFIED beyond the abstract].
- McClellan, R., stability of trapezoidally discretised time-varying virtual-analog filters, DAFx 2026, paper 28. https://www.dafx.de/paper-archive/2026/papers/DAFx26_paper_28.pdf — search snippet only [UNVERIFIED].
- Simper, A. (Cytomic), "Solving the continuous SVF equations using trapezoidal integration and equivalent currents" — source of the SVF recurrence form used here; the recurrence was verified against its closed-form response in the model. Document not re-read in this stage.
- Bristow-Johnson, R., Audio EQ Cookbook. https://www.w3.org/TR/audio-eq-cookbook/ — analog prototypes for the bell and the second-order shelf.
- Repo: `research/parametric-eq-filter-design.md` (2026-03-07). Built on for prototypes and the cramping problem. Two of its statements are superseded here: its section 9.3 "matched bandwidth" code is the plain bilinear SVF (it still cramps), and its recommendation of `StateVariableTPTFilter` as the best balance does not meet DSP-01.

### Professional plugins
- FabFilter Pro-Q 3 / 4 (benchmark named in the brief), DMG EQuilibrium, Kirchhoff-EQ, TDR Nova. Their internal filter designs are proprietary; no behaviour claim in this document rests on them. Workflow conventions referenced (curve-first editing, per-band placement, band listen, auto gain, Q 1 = flat cut) are from general product knowledge and are [UNVERIFIED] in detail.
- O-AnalogEQ 1.5.7 (sibling): reused for build layout, preset-manager wiring, 30 Hz meter timer, render-harness pattern, layout refusal of asymmetric buses. Not reused: its RBJ `IIR::Filter` bands and the coloured `analog-eq-unit` module.

## Notes

- The Stage 0 model scripts are scratch files and are not part of the repo. Phase 2.1 re-implements the model as the offline designer harness; the tables in "Model results" are its acceptance values.
- Design Sync: no mockup exists, so there is nothing to compare. Differences from the draft spec that the mockup must adopt: `analyzer` is UI state (196 host parameters, not 197); IDs are zero-padded `bNN_`; global block first; slope control disabled for Bell, Notch, Band Pass; Q control disabled at 6 dB/oct; gain control disabled for cuts, notch, band pass.
- French and zh-Hans: type, slope and placement choice strings are host-visible parameter values and stay English in the parameter; the page localises its own labels.
